output.summary: An annual or biennial herb native to Europe, much of Asia, and parts of Africa, hairy bittercress commonly grows in damp, disturbed ground. Its ripe upright pods burst when touched, flinging seeds away. The leaves, flowers and seedpods are eaten raw or cooked and taste mildly peppery; the seeds can replace mustard.
output.edibilityNote: Leaves, flowers and seedpods are eaten raw or cooked; leaves are used in salads, and seeds can substitute for mustard.
